- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 5–7% below peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for next 7–14 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–2% per day for first 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
